findings.claim: The script uses the BSD/macOS-only `sed -i '' -E` syntax, which fails on GNU sed (Linux). When it fails, the .env update does not happen but the script still prints that GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL was updated.

verifier.reason: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:68 uses BSD/macOS `sed -i '' -E`, which fails on GNU sed (treating `''` as an empty script and the substitution expression as a filename) without updating `$ENV_FILE`. Because the script has no `set -e` or exit-status check, it still prints the success message at scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:73.

findings.claim: After the deleteCache mutation in CredentialActionsDropdown succeeds, it only calls onSuccess and does not invalidate viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. Callers that pass no onSuccess, such as EventAdvancedTab, then show a stale cacheUpdatedAt / 'Last updated'.

verifier.reason: In packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:42-50, deleteCacheMutation only calls showToast and onSuccess?.() without invalidating utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars (unlike disconnectMutation at lines 61-64). SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx:71-78,124-131 forwards props.onChanged as onSuccess using data from connectedCalendars.useQuery (lines 153-161), and EventAdvancedTab.tsx:372-384 renders SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper without onChanged, leaving cacheUpdatedAt and 'Last updated' stale after cache deletion.

findings.claim: SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) is called with empty data. With updateMany in Prisma 5.4.2 this does not bump @updatedAt, nothing reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, and the call adds an extra UPDATE on every fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache run.

verifier.reason: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1024, fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}), which invokes prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany with empty data in packages/lib/server/repository/selectedCalendar.ts:400-405; with Prisma 5.4.2 (packages/prisma/package.json) this does not bump @updatedAt on SelectedCalendar (packages/prisma/schema.prisma:860) and adds a redundant database call on every run. Furthermore, the cache status UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt via packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts:28-36 and packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:173-188, and nothing reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt even where selected in packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts:899.

findings.claim: The cache 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, which ignores the user's locale (i18n.language from useLocale) and profile timezone.

verifier.reason: In packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:88-94, the `cache_last_updated` timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })`, hard-coding the locale instead of using `i18n.language` from `useLocale()` (only `t` is destructured on line 37) and omitting any `timeZone` option for the user's profile timezone.

findings.claim: dev:cron switches from ts-node to `npx tsx`, but tsx is not declared as a dependency and is not in yarn.lock. npx therefore downloads it from the registry at run time.

verifier.reason: apps/web/package.json:11 changes dev:cron from ts-node to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, while tsx is not declared in apps/web/package.json or root package.json and has no entry in yarn.lock (between tsutils at yarn.lock:45184 and tty-browserify at yarn.lock:45196). Consequently, npx has no locally installed tsx binary and downloads it unpinned from the registry at run time.

findings.claim: prisma.credential.findFirst has no select, so it loads the full Credential row, including the key (OAuth tokens), only to check existence and ownership.

verifier.reason: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:17-26, prisma.credential.findFirst is called without a select clause and the result is only checked for truthiness, so Prisma fetches the entire Credential row including the key JSON column (OAuth tokens) defined in packages/prisma/schema.prisma:222-226.

findings.claim: The mock getCacheStatusByCredentialIds does not accept the credentialIds parameter, so it does not match the interface signature.

verifier.reason: In packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts:27, getCacheStatusByCredentialIds() declares no parameters, unlike ICalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(credentialIds: number[]) in packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.interface.ts:30-32. TypeScript still allows omitting unused parameters when implementing an interface (matching the other methods in CalendarCacheRepositoryMock), so this only fails type-checking if invoked directly on a CalendarCacheRepositoryMock-typed instance.
